A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Ariadne maze-based RLVR study. Their text, equations, tables and figures are readable and support comparison. v1 has no appendix; v4's Appendix A.1–A.4 is included in this assessment.

before.justification: v1 reports original training and evaluation results for Ariadne on AlphaMaze, MapBench and ReasonMap, including quantitative comparisons and navigation examples.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and adds SFT comparisons, sampling-budget evaluations and additional model-scale results, including appendix results.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure retains GRPO, the inverted-Gaussian maze curriculum, turn-scaled full/prefix-match rewards with weights 0.2/0.1, and the navigation prompt. v4 corrects the displayed GRPO equation, assessed under T1, but reports no new algorithmic component or change to the implemented procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use AlphaMaze, the same nine MapBench environments, and short/long ReasonMap questions. Maze training remains limited to 1–5 moves and 0–2 turns, with evaluation extending to 10 moves and 4 turns. Additional sampling and model-size analyses do not establish new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v4 adds a supervised fine-tuned control trained on the same AlphaMaze data and initialization to the MapBench and ReasonMap comparisons. v1 compares only the base Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct model with Ariadne. This adds an important alternative training method against which RLVR is evaluated.

E3.justification: v4 introduces pass@k coverage evaluation through k=1024, intermediate-budget evaluations in Appendix A.3, and trajectory comparisons with N=128 at temperature 1.0. It also evaluates Qwen2.5-VL-3B and Qwen3-VL-4B/8B. These substantially expand evaluation design beyond v1's 7B experiments; they do not establish that retained benchmark results were rerun.

E4.justification: v4 adds sampling-budget sensitivity, cross-model-size checks, and MapBench success distributions by path length. Sampled base/Ariadne trajectory comparisons replace v1's labeled maze success/failure examples and trail/museum case studies. Appendix A.3 additionally examines whether coverage trends persist with finer sampling-budget resolution.

E5.justification: v1 explicitly specifies eight independent evaluation rollouts for AlphaMaze and MapBench. v4 describes averaging independent rollouts across all three benchmarks but omits their count for these aggregate evaluations. Neither version reports training seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests; the new pass@k budgets concern evaluation design.

E6.justification: v4 adds extensive SFT, model-scale and coverage results; for example, Table 1 reports 41.0% six-step coverage for Ariadne at k=1024 versus 0.0% for the base model. Maze success results and some ReasonMap figure values are revised: Figure 6's easy/easy long-question base Map Score changes from 6.10 to 13.94, while Ariadne remains 12.81. The original aggregate base/Ariadne MapBench and ReasonMap table entries are retained unchanged.

T1.justification: v4 Equation (3) restores advantage factors A_i in both terms of the clipped GRPO surrogate, which v1 Equation (2) omitted. This corrects the written mathematical objective. The curriculum and reward equations are otherwise equivalent, and no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: v1 claims boundary extension but concludes that RLVR may only strengthen patterns learned during pretraining. v4 explicitly claims to refute the efficiency-only explanation and to induce novel spatial behaviors or primitives beyond the base policy's effective support. Its conclusion also extends the claimed generality across model scales.

C2.justification: v4 introduces soft/hard support regimes, explains dense rewards as enabling escape from zero success, and interprets real-world transfer as trajectory-density spillover with softer boundaries. It adds limitations concerning the maze proxy, restricted model scales and transfer of exact complexity boundaries. Pretraining opacity and eventual failure at high complexity were already acknowledged in v1.

D1.justification: v4 adds the SFT control's matching data, initialization and training-setting disclosures. It omits v1's detailed maze distribution counts, ReasonMap difficulty-group sample counts, and some parsing and metric-validation details. Hardware and principal hyperparameters remain documented, and the unchanged system prompt moves to Appendix A.2.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially repositioned around RLVR efficiency versus capability expansion. v4 adds works such as Yue et al., Zhao et al.'s Echo Chamber, and contamination studies by Matton and Liang, while removing several earlier VLM and navigation references, including Flamingo and CoT-VLA. Ariadne becomes an explicit counterpoint to the efficiency hypothesis.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, method exposition and conclusions are extensively rewritten around the efficiency/capability question. Curriculum material moves into the method section, the prompt moves to an appendix, and separate limitations and appendix sections are introduced. This is substantial narrative restructuring beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: The document changes from one-column to two-column layout, restructures existing tables, and adds coverage and model-scale displays. Dataset-distribution histograms disappear, maze case displays are reworked, and Figure 6 gains SFT bars and revised category labels. v1's benchmark illustration is split and relocated to Appendix Figures 8–9 rather than representing new benchmark coverage.

improvement.justification: The matched SFT control, sampling through k=1024 and additional model sizes substantially strengthen empirical checks missing from v1. However, v4 replaces v1's cautious mechanism caveat with categorical novel-primitive and zero-support claims that finite sampling cannot establish. Its persistent-superiority narrative also conflicts with counterexamples in Table 4 and Figure 6, including the base model's 13.94 versus Ariadne's 12.81 easy/easy long-question Map Score. These empirical benefits and worsened claim/evidence alignment leave the net quality change uncertain.
